evals.prompt: The brief asks for a scroll-driven 3D hero: a GLB product model that rotates as the user scrolls, on a landing page whose LCP target is 2.5 s.
evals.expected_output: Lazily mounts a single clamped-DPR canvas behind a poster, drives rotation from a gsap.context ScrollTrigger timeline animating transform/opacity only, compresses the GLB (Draco/Meshopt) under ~2 MB or defers it past first paint, and ships a reduced-motion static branch plus a no-WebGL poster fallback.

evals.prompt: A card asks for a Blender-modeled hero prop with custom lighting, rendered into the site, and the scene also needs scripted exports on every content change.
evals.expected_output: Asks the card's requester for the heavy render instead of rendering it in the site repo, uses glTF with baked lighting and KTX2/Draco compression, and treats the confirm-gated blender plugin as a build-time tool only when scripted Blender work is required (after the user's OK), never as part of the shipped bundle.

evals.prompt: A preview FIX round reports the animated page janks on mid-range mobile and users with motion sensitivity cannot read the scroll story.
evals.expected_output: Measures the preview URL first, removes per-frame allocations and layout-triggering properties, batches ScrollTrigger, then makes the reduced-motion branch a complete static version of the same content (no Lenis, no hijack) and records the measured LCP/INP in the card.
